Thanks, Elena. I'll start with what I'm seeing on my end. On the positive side, several team members have explicitly asked for longer uninterrupted work periods, and there's genuine enthusiasm for the idea of a day with no recurring internal meetings. That's a real signal that people are struggling with context-switching and fragmentation.

On the constraint side, the main concern is handoffs. We have several workflows that depend on live touchpoints between teams throughout the week, and if we pull one weekday entirely out of the recurring meeting calendar, we need to think carefully about how coordination still happens reliably. There's a worry -- and I share it -- that fewer live touchpoints could make some of our cross-team coordination feel less respectful and less reliable, especially for people who depend on quick clarifications.
